characters.name: Hermes
characters.register_notes: Fast-talking, always on edge, like George Costanza.

characters.name: Charon
characters.register_notes: Petty DMV-clerk style, annoyed by the mundane.

bible.narrative_arc: Hermes tries to settle a debt with Charon, who is unable to pay due to a lack of business.
bible.tempo_envelope: Fast-paced with a comedic rhythm, reflecting the sitcom style.
key_beats: Charon reluctantly agrees to Hermes' list of expenses.
Charon admits he can't pay due to low business.
Hermes laments the change in clientele from warriors to weaklings.
Charon and Hermes reflect on the current state of souls.
bible.directorial_notes: Focus on the comedic tension between Hermes' impatience and Charon's bureaucratic excuses. Keep the dialogue snappy and emphasize the absurdity of their situation.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: <emotion value="frustrated"/> Hey Charon, let's settle up what you owe me, so we don't end up arguing about it again.

lines.speaker: Charon
lines.text: <emotion value="frustrated"/> Sure thing, Hermes. It's better to have it all clear and avoid any hassle.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: <emotion value="frustrated"/> I brought you an anchor for five drachmas.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: <emotion value="frustrated"/> By Hades, I paid five for it, plus two obols for the rope.

lines.speaker: Charon
lines.text: <emotion value="frustrated"/> Fine, put down five drachmas and two obols.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: <emotion value="frustrated"/> And I paid five obols for a sail patch.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: <emotion value="frustrated"/> And wax to seal the leaks in your boat, plus nails and a cord for the rudder, all for two drachmas.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: <emotion value="frustrated"/> That's everything, unless we forgot something. So, when are you going to pay up?

lines.speaker: Charon
lines.text: <emotion value="frustrated"/> Right now, it's impossible, Hermes. But if a plague or war sends a bunch of souls our way, I'll make enough to cover the fare.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: <emotion value="frustrated"/> So, I'm supposed to sit here hoping for the worst just to get paid?

lines.speaker: Charon
lines.text: <emotion value="frustrated"/> That's the way it is, Hermes. Not many are coming down here now, as you can see. It's peace time.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: <emotion value="frustrated"/> Well, it'd be nice if you could extend the debt a bit. But you know, Charon, back in the day, the souls were all warriors, covered in blood and wounds. Now they're all pale, weaklings, poisoned by their kids or wives, or just bloated from indulgence. They're nothing like the old ones. Most of them are here because they were plotting against each other for money.

lines.speaker: Charon
lines.text: <emotion value="frustrated"/> Yeah, those things are really in demand.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: <emotion value="frustrated"/> So you can't blame me for being a bit pushy about getting what's owed.

annotation.notes: The dialogue captures the comedic tension between Hermes' impatience and Charon's bureaucratic excuses, maintaining a fast-paced, sitcom-style rhythm.
